answer:
You don't pass a separate registry option. You put the registry reference directly in the `scan-model` path argument, and set credentials through environment variables.

**MLflow:** Use a `models:/` URI as the path. The docs give this example: "promptfoo scan-model models:/MyModel/Latest" [promptfoo/site/docs/model-audit/usage.md]. The server address comes from the environment: "- `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`: The URI of your MLflow tracking server." [promptfoo/site/docs/model-audit/usage.md]. Credentials are set with `MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME` and `MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD` [promptfoo/site/docs/model-audit/usage.md]. Scanning MLflow also requires the mlflow package: "pip install mlflow" [promptfoo/site/docs/model-audit/index.md].

**JFrog Artifactory:** Pass the full artifact URL as the path. The docs show "promptfoo scan-model "https://your-domain.jfrog.io/artifactory/repo/model.pkl"" [promptfoo/site/docs/model-audit/usage.md]. Set the base URL and token first: "- `JFROG_URL`: The base URL of your JFrog Artifactory instance." and "- `JFROG_API_TOKEN` or `JFROG_ACCESS_TOKEN`: Your API or access token." [promptfoo/site/docs/model-audit/usage.md]

Note that the JFrog ML provider (for inference) is a different product from JFrog Artifactory, which is what ModelAudit scans [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/jfrog.md].

The context doesn't show a dedicated flag for selecting a registry, so I don't know of one.
